key_insight: SOTAlign shows that frozen unimodal vision and language models can be meaningfully aligned using a semi‑supervised optimal transport objective, achieving strong cross‑modal alignment with substantially fewer paired examples than contrastive-only methods.
problem_solved: Reducing the heavy reliance on millions of paired image–text samples for aligning pretrained vision and language encoders by enabling effective alignment from a small set of paired examples plus abundant unpaired data.
method: Keep pretrained vision and language backbones frozen and add lightweight alignment heads that map each modality into a shared space.

Use a semi‑supervised training objective that combines a small supervised pairing loss (for available image–text pairs) with an optimal transport (OT) alignment term computed on unpaired batches to match empirical distributions across modalities.
Solve OT with an entropic regularization (e.g., Sinkhorn) for efficient, differentiable coupling estimates and integrate the resulting transport plan as a supervision signal for the alignment layers.
impact: Enables practitioners to align large unimodal models for multimodal tasks with far fewer paired examples, lowering data collection costs and making cross‑modal transfer and retrieval feasible in low‑label regimes.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen ViT and frozen LLM/text encoder feeding lightweight alignment heads into a shared embedding space.
Optimal transport schematic: two point clouds (vision, language) with transport arrows and a heatmap of the transport plan/coupling matrix.
Performance curve: retrieval or alignment metric vs. number of paired samples, showing SOTAlign maintaining performance with much fewer pairs.
Pipeline icon set: 'Frozen models' icon, 'Small heads' icon, 'Few pairs + many unpaired' icon, and a 'Sinkhorn/OT' algorithm icon.
paper_title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
paper_authors: Simon Roschmann, Paul Krzakala, Sonia Mazelet, Quentin Bouniot, Zeynep Akata
